The Borough President has 30 days after the Community Board issues a recommendation to review the application and issue a recommendation.

attributes.dcp-consideration:
Brooklyn Community Board 6 voted to approve the ULURP application for the Red Hook Coastal Resiliency(RHCR) project at our February 21st, 2024, full board meeting. Twenty-six were in favor, zero opposed, and one abstention. However, the approval is conditional on various factors based on the Red Hook community’s concerns. 

The first condition is that the data used for the decisions be updated to reflect the current reality of flooding in Red Hook. While the impetus for this project stems from Sandy, the reality has shifted in the wrong direction since, so the planning should reflect that. Additionally, the RHCR should not exclude several large buildings, small businesses, and a supermarket at the end of Van Brunt Street. The community must be regularly and actively engaged, informed, and consulted as it deals with the reality and needs for resiliency in Red Hook in real-time. As such, the Red Hook’s input will result in a better, and therefore more resilient, RHCR.

attributes.dcp-publichearinglocation: Brooklyn Borough Hall, 209 Joralemon Street Brooklyn, NY 11201
attributes.dcp-consideration: Please see attached memo for full comment.

attributes.dcp-projectbrief: The Department of Design and Construction, Department of Transportation, Department of Citywide Administrative Services, and Department of Parks and Recreation are seeking City Map amendments to regrade and elevate several streets and map new parkland to enlarge Todd Triangle Park, as well as acquisitions related to easements along private property, to facilitate a neighborhood-wide flood resiliency project in Red Hook, Community District 6, Brooklyn.
